author: Russell Brand
description:
Matthew McConaughey opened by sharing results from a survey of thousands of thirteen year old girls asked how they wanted to become famous, and the leading answer was deeply unsettling, revealing just how skewed the culture's values around fame and money have become. He argued this isn't really about any one generation's failure, it's about a system that rewards being a valuable commodity and discards anyone who doesn't fit that mold, reinforced by institutions meant to prepare kids for life. Russell reflected on his own faith as a way of pushing back against that framework entirely, trying to access eternal principles like honor, integrity, decency, and kindness instead of chasing whatever the culture currently rewards. Sometimes the most radical thing you can do is refuse to play by those rules.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest opened by detailing how a major charitable research funder made around ten billion dollars during the pandemic due to its heavy investment in pharmaceutical companies and even a food delivery service, while the person leading that organization was simultaneously pushing hard for lockdowns. He connected this directly to a heavily flawed modeling paper out of a research institute also funded by a major foundation, a paper that predicted millions of deaths without lockdowns and was cited by health officials to justify closing down entire countries. He pointed out that the underlying computer code behind those catastrophic predictions was never peer reviewed or publicly disclosed, despite being the basis for decisions that reshaped the world. Russell let the numbers speak for themselves.
